name: Abiram
overview: Abiram was a male member of the tribe of Reuben known for his rebellion against Moses alongside Korah. His defiance is a notable example of opposition to God-ordained leadership during the wilderness period. There are no additional personal notes recorded about him beyond this act of rebellion.
namesAndTitles: The name Abiram means '[my] father is exalted,' reflecting a Hebrew proper name with no indication that it was given directly by God. This meaning suggests a recognition of exaltation, though the biblical account focuses primarily on his actions rather than the significance of his name.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records that Abiram was the son of Eliab. No other family relationships are explicitly mentioned in the biblical text beyond this paternal connection.
scriptureSignificance: Abiram's significance in the biblical narrative centers on his role in the rebellion against Moses, challenging the divinely appointed leadership during Israel's wilderness journey. His participation in this insurrection highlights the dangers of opposing God's chosen servants and serves as a warning against rebellion. This event marks him as a cautionary figure within the history of Israel's formative experiences under God's guidance.
